chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Isḥāq ibn Yazīd, from Mihrān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, and a number of others, said:
We were seated in the presence of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said:

A servant does not deserve the reality of faith until death is more beloved to him than life, and illness is more beloved to him than health, and poverty is more beloved to him than wealth. So are you like this?
So we said, 'No, by Allah! May Allah make us sacrificed for you.' And they dropped into their hands, and despair fell into their hearts.
So when he saw what had entered them from that, he said: 'Is it pleasing to one of you that he lives as long as he lives, then dies upon other than this matter, or he dies upon what he is upon?'
We said, 'Rather, he dies upon what he is upon at this time.'
He said: 'So I see that death is more beloved to you than life.'
Then he said: 'Is it pleasing to one of you that he remains as long as he remains, not struck by anything from these illnesses and pains, until he dies upon other than this matter?'
We said, 'No, O son of the Messenger of Allah.'
He said: 'So I see that illness is more beloved to you than health.'
Then he said: 'Is it pleasing to one of you that he has all that the sun rises upon, and he is upon other than this matter?'
We said, 'No, O son of the Messenger of Allah.'
He said: 'So I see that poverty is more beloved to you than wealth.'

key_terms.حَقِيقَةَ الْإِيمَانِ: The reality or essence of faith

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to prefer death over life in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that true faith (ḥaqīqat al-īmān) is not merely the presence of death, illness, or poverty, but the preference for these states when they align with Wilayah and divine pleasure. He addresses the companions' initial despair by distinguishing between the burden of the condition and the spiritual reality it signifies, confirming that their preference for dying in a state of faith over prolonged life without it validates their sincere belief. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the internal disposition (niyyah) and the value of enduring trials as a means of spiritual purification and closeness to God.
